name: bluewater-shorts-63-72
lines: One of these texts just lost the job.
A customer writes, hi, how much to fix a leaking tap?
Reply A. One fifty. Send me your address.
Reply B. Depends. Is it dripping, or spraying? I can come look tomorrow at ten.
Lock in your answer. Three. Two. One.
It was A. He answered her question, and lost.
Because the guy before him said one forty.
B never gave a number. He gave a time.
A number starts a price war. A question starts a job.
Something on this listing is killing his phone.
You have five seconds. Find it.
Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
Did you say the three point nine stars? Wrong.
The logo instead of a photo? Close. But no.
It's this. Open twenty four hours.
He is not open twenty four hours. He is asleep.
So at two a.m., a flooded basement calls him. And nobody picks up.
Then she writes the review. Said open. Wasn't.
One lie on your listing writes its own one star.
Ranking contractor lies. Number one is a crime.
Number five. I'm ten minutes away. He is in his kitchen. Eating.
Number four. It's a quick fix. It has never, in history, been a quick fix.
Number three. I'll send the quote tonight. Which night? He didn't say.
Number two. The last guy did this all wrong. The last guy was him.
And number one.
We don't need a contract. I'm a handshake guy.
That's not a lie. That's a confession.
Be the boring one. Show up. Write it down. Text back.
She just asked for a discount. You have three answers.
Two of them cost you money.
Answer one. Sure, I'll knock off ten percent. Congratulations. You just told her your price was made up.
Answer two. No. That's the price. Strong. Also, she's gone.
Answer three.
Sure. Which part should we take out?
Watch her face. She doesn't want less work. She wants to feel like she won.
So keep the price, and throw in something small.
Never cut the price. Cut the scope.
I am a contractor's voicemail.
I've been full for three years.
People still call. I tell them I'm full. They believe me.
Last week, a woman called about a whole new kitchen.
I heard everything. The budget. The deadline. The hope in her voice.
Then I said, the mailbox is full. Goodbye.
He thinks business is slow. It's not slow. It's in here. With me.
Twenty nine messages. He will never hear one.
Delete me. Please. I'm begging you.
Four fifty nine. Friday. The phone rings.
Do you answer? Decide now.
Behind door one. A man whose toilet has been running since April. He'd like it fixed tonight. For free. He knows your cousin.
Behind door two. A property manager. Forty units. Her plumber just quit.
Same ring. Same number. You cannot tell them apart.
So here's what you do.
You answer. And you say the nine best words in business.
I'm done for today. Can I call you Monday?
The toilet guy hangs up. The property manager says, Monday's perfect.
You don't have to work Friday night. You just have to pick up.
Right before she calls you, she searches five things.
One. Your name. Fine.
Two. Your name, plus reviews. Okay.
Three. Your name, plus scam. Just checking.
Four. Your face. She wants to know who's walking into her house.
And five.
The other guy. She has him open in the next tab. Right now.
You're not being judged. You're being compared.
So whatever she finds on him, make sure she finds more on you.
Losing a customer. Speed run. Go.
Zero seconds. She calls. He watches it ring.
Two seconds. Voicemail. Full.
Four seconds. She texts. He replies, who's this?
Six seconds. She explains. He says, call me.
She is the one who called him.
Eight seconds. She asks the price. He sends, depends.
Nine point six. She hires the other guy. New world record.
Every step felt normal. That's the scary part.
Slow it down. Pick up. Use her name. Give her a time.
Pause to see which customer you get today.
Three. Two. One. Pause.
Whoever you got, here's the cheat code.
The Haggler wants a win. Give a small extra. Never a discount.
The Ghost needs a deadline. I'm holding Thursday for you until five.
The Night Texter gets a reply at eight a.m. Not at midnight.
And if you got the Unicorn, who pays the deposit the same day? Screenshot it. Nobody will believe you.
Comment who you got.
What your business name says about you.
Triple A anything. You picked it for the phone book. There is no phone book.
Your last name, and sons. The sons have other plans.
Anything with elite, premier, or pro. Bold. Unverified.
A pun. You're either the funniest guy in town, or the only one laughing.
Your initials. J and R services. What services, J and R? Nobody knows.
And the winner. Your town, plus what you do.
Boring. Clear. She knows what you do before she clicks.
Nobody hires the clever one. They hire the one they understood.
